beginner.summary: For system administrators, DevOps engineers and developers who manage Linux or Windows servers and are new to Chef. Covers installing Chef Workstation, the Chef Infra Language and core resources, cookbooks, recipes, templates, attributes and Ohai, notifications and guards, local testing with Test Kitchen, Chef InSpec and Cookstyle, Chef Infra Server organizations, knife bootstrapping, run lists, roles and environments, a first Policyfile, data bags, reading failed chef-client runs, and a web server cookbook capstone.
prerequisites: Administers Linux servers from the command line: packages, services, files, permissions and SSH keys
Reads and edits simple Ruby or another scripting language and uses Git for version control
Has a laptop with rights to install Chef Workstation, Docker or Vagrant with VirtualBox, and SSH access to at least one disposable Linux VM
outcomes: Write idempotent recipes with core Chef Infra resources, templates, attributes, notifications and guards
Generate, lint and test cookbooks locally with chef generate, Cookstyle, Test Kitchen and Chef InSpec
Bootstrap nodes to a Chef Infra Server with knife and assign configuration through run lists, roles, environments or a Policyfile
Read a chef-client run log, locate the failing resource and fix the cookbook so the next run converges with zero errors

intermediate.summary: For engineers who already write and test basic cookbooks and bootstrap nodes to a Chef Infra Server, and now need to build reusable, well-tested Chef code for teams. Covers custom resources, libraries, the compile and converge phases, ChefSpec unit tests, multi-suite Test Kitchen, search, Chef Vault, encrypted data bags and the secret helper, Policyfile groups and promotion, wrapper cookbooks, Windows nodes, Ohai plugins, handlers, chef-client scheduling, the Compliance Phase with InSpec profiles, a cookbook CI pipeline, and a multi-tier Policyfile capstone.
prerequisites: Has completed the Chef beginner level or writes cookbooks with templates, attributes, notifications and InSpec tests

Reads Ruby classes, modules and blocks and uses Git with pull requests and a CI service such as GitHub Actions
outcomes: Build custom resources and libraries that are idempotent, documented and unit-tested with ChefSpec

advanced.summary: For senior infrastructure engineers, Chef platform owners and consultants who run Chef for hundreds or thousands of nodes. Covers Chef Infra Server design, backup and restore, tuning and security hardening, Chef Automate deployment, compliance scanning, infra views and data feeds, custom InSpec resources and waivers, Chef Habitat at awareness level, Target Mode, run performance profiling, release rings with Policyfiles, testing custom resources at scale, Chef Infra Client and Server upgrades, deprecation clean-up with Cookstyle, migration from roles, environments and Berkshelf to Policyfiles, server-to-server migration, fleet compliance remediation, monitoring, and an upgrade-and-migration capstone.
prerequisites: Has completed the Chef intermediate level or builds custom resources, ChefSpec tests and Policyfile promotions for a team
Administers Linux servers, PostgreSQL basics, TLS certificates and load balancers in production
Has access to lab VMs or a cloud account able to run a Chef Infra Server, a Chef Automate instance and at least five managed nodes
outcomes: Operate, back up, tune and harden Chef Infra Server and Chef Automate for a large fleet
Deliver compliance scanning, waivers and remediation across Linux and Windows nodes with Chef InSpec and Chef Automate
Plan and execute Chef Infra Client and Chef Infra Server upgrades, removing deprecations with Cookstyle and ChefSpec
Migrate an estate from roles, environments and Berkshelf to Policyfiles, or between Chef Infra Servers, without configuration drift
